about: Client-side cases for interactive messages (kind hypertext): the pure card logic (frontend/src/hypertext/bindings.ts, ported to Kotlin core/Hypertext.kt and Swift AcerciaeCore/Hypertext.swift) and the script engine with its host validation (engine.ts + effects.ts, the mobile bundle mobile/contracts/hypertext/hypertext-engine.js). The cases shared with the C++ backend (defaults, state_validation, conditions, interpolation, dice_policy) live in hypertext.json.

A case's "doc" names an entry of "docs" (the public document as stored in messages.hypertext). For "runs", "script" replaces the doc's script (null: no script), and "prev" (default: "state") is the state before the binding change.
bindings: applyAction(doc, state, node, action) gives expect {state, event}, or null when the action does not apply.
resolve: resolve(doc, state, lock) lists every node in document order, projected as {type, id (null without one), text?, label?, caption?, value?, options?, visible, disabled}.
act: act(doc, state, node) gives expect {state, effects}, or null.

runs: the engine output after host validation. expect.ok true compares only the fields given (state, effects, notices, logs, confirm, changed); expect.ok false gives the error code (and line or logs when given).

parseDoc fills in what the server's normalize fills in (title "", label = value, text style body and tone neutral, choice display list, button style primary, enum default null, script and actors null, runs_per_viewer 1, closes_at null, replies [], a stub's slots {}, audience card, group null) and keeps act.say ASCII-trimmed; so a post body reads like the stored card. Shared hypertext.json cases are read as the C++ tests read them: a state_decl case is {v:1, state: state_decl, body:[{type:divider}]} (conditions put cond in its show_if), and state_validation and conditions use the case's state as given (missing keys take their defaults).

bindings: a case may give "lock" (default {reason: null}); action commit (an input's draft on blur) gives event null. resolve also disables a button whose act replies while a slot cannot be filled from the state.

runs: a runner passes prev = state when the case gives none (prev is required by MobileHypertext and client.ts). The engine's deadline_ms is checked at each interrupt poll (code timeout); the hosts end a run that does not answer within timeout_ms (cold_timeout_ms for a new worker).

Location: these sections (engine limits for the client, bindings, resolve, act, runs) are planned for hypertext.json; they live here while the backend phase writes that file, so that the two phases do not edit one file. Merge them into hypertext.json then, and reconcile its engine section with this one (stack_bytes 131072, deadline_ms, the version string).
